answer: That prevents an operator from swapping in a better text after seeing what peers submitted, which is the main advantage of running many keys. Because the reef commitment is timestamped in the lotus ledger, the terrace audit verifies the pair and a late swap fails the hash. The answer is committed as a 215 bit hash at open and revealed at close, and a reveal that does not match the commitment is void. Verification alone takes 1 days each. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
